text:
alan: Heads-up — saw a big 95th/99th latency spike during the morning hosted load test. nsys trace suggests repeated kernel compiles on cold path for a variant we rolled yesterday. attaching quick summary.

alan: ```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=nvtx,cuda python perf/load_test.py

Timeline excerpt (normalized):
[0.120s] triton::compile_kernel(model=llama-13b-q4, op=matmul, seq=1024)  -> 110ms
[0.245s] triton::compile_kernel(model=llama-13b-q4, op=softmax, seq=1024)  -> 95ms
[0.360s] cudaLaunchKernel(matmul_kernel)  -> 0.9ms
[0.362s] cudaLaunchKernel(softmax_kernel) -> 0.6ms
[0.480s] triton::compile_kernel(model=llama-13b-q4, op=matmul, seq=256)   -> 118ms
[0.610s] triton::cache_insert(kcache_key=...) -> 2ms
```

nora: Which test? single long-seq clients or mixed batch?

alan: Mixed. 70% short (seq<=128) and 30% long (seq>=1024). The runtime mixes shapes into a few batches which triggers specialized kernels for the long seqs.

kevin: Do we have numbers for how many unique kernels got jitted per minute? sounds like cache churn.

alan: From the trace: ~42 unique kernel compiles in the first 60s, many for matmul variants. The kernel cache hit rate was ~45% initially, then stabilizes to ~90% after warmup.

marta: Can you paste the kcache metadata from the runtime? eviction policy, TTL, and max entries?

alan: ```
KCache config:
max_entries=512
eviction=LIFO
entry_ttl=600s
cur_entries=198
insert_rate=0.7/s
```

kevin: LIFO is suspicious for mixed workloads. If long-shape compiles are interleaved they evict older long-shape entries. That explains the hot/cold churn. Suggest switching to LRU or adding shape-binning before insertion.

marta: Agree. Also two ideas: (1) precompile bins for common seq lengths at model upload (2) fallback selector: on cold-path prefer generic kernels with lower compile cost and slightly worse per-op latency, to avoid 100ms compile spikes.

alan: Perfetto flamegraph (aggregated over 2m) shows ~3.2s spent in triton::compile_kernel across the timeline, contributing ~60ms median tail across requests during warmup.

profiling-bot: dashboard: https://internal.redwood/prof/1876543210 : shows compile latency breakdown and per-shard counts.

infra-bot: load test run id 2026-03-17-09: config attached. CPU/GPU utilization normal, no OOMs.

nora: Is this specific to q4 quantized variant? we saw earlier that quant kernels sometimes generate more shader variants.

alan: Yes, only reproduced on q4 variant. fp16 doesn't show compile surge.

kevin: Action proposal:
- short term: flip kcache eviction to LRU and increase max_entries to 1024 (marta)
- medium: implement selector fallback path for first N requests (kevin)
- longer: precompile common bins at model upload (marta + runtime)

marta: I'll own the LRU + size bump. Running a canary tonight.

alan: I'll re-run nsys with the canary and post the before/after timelines.

kevin: If canary looks good, let's roll to dedicated fleets. Also add a perf test that mixes seq distributions to catch regressions.

marta: noted. created an issue: https://jira/redwood/browse/ENGRT-4621 (owner=marta, due=next-wed)

alan: Thanks everyone. Please react with :eyes: when you see the updated traces.
